title: Control Plane: weekly handover + routing/auth checkpoints
content:
Summary

Quick handover for the week of 2026-12-22. This doc is a lightweight record of what the control plane rota is tracking, short updates from routing/auth/quotas owners, and the immediate follow-ups for the next oncall rotation. Meeting was informal; notes include action items and open questions.

Attendees
- Aisha Patel (owner, control plane)
- Liam Chen (routing)
- Sofia Martinez (auth & IAM)
- Diego Ruiz (quotas / throttling)
- Priya Nair (SRE / incident responder)
- Notes: joined late: Maria K. (10m)

Goals for this session
- Quick sync on any regressions or alerts that need prolonged attention
- Confirm routing experiments (allocation changes) for Canary A/B next Tue
- Handoff any outstanding quota throttling sprints to next rotation

Recent signals / metrics (past 7 days)
- Control plane API p50: 38ms, p95: 210ms (trend: p95 up ~12% week-over-week)
- Throttle triggered count: avg 420/day, spike 1.8k on 12/19 (mid-day) tied to a bursty customer job
- Auth 401 error rate: 0.18% (baseline 0.05%) — spike correlated with a token-service restart on 12/17
- Route allocation loss events: 3 pod evictions due to OOM on n1-standard-32 nodes (non-GPU controlplane)
- Incident noise: 2 P2 pagers (one resolved by rollback of PR 389, one ongoing investigation)

Round-robin updates
1) Control plane (Aisha)
- PR 389 rollback reduced error noise; root cause likely a race in cache invalidation around model variant metadata. Follow-up PR created to add stronger invalidation guard (WIP).
- Rolling restart plan for controlplane services tomorrow morning (small-window). SRE signed off for midnight wave.
- TODO: Add more granular logging around variant cache misses (owner: Aisha, due: 2026-12-24).

2) Routing (Liam)
- Canary A/B for new allocator policy scheduled for 2026-12-28. Two keys: (a) reduce cross-zone routing when latency diff > 60ms; (b) prefer cheaper compatible variant when spare capacity low.
- Need to add a metric to track requests routed to fallback variants (owner: Liam, due: 2026-12-26). Current dashboards don't split fallback vs primary clearly.
- Observed an increase in 502 responses at regional edge — likely related to env mismatch in a new sidecar. Follow-up: sidecar image pin and redeploy in staging (PR: ROUTE-1308).

3) Auth & IAM (Sofia)
- Token-service incident 12/17: partial outage during key rotation. We fixed the rotation script and added a canary group to validate new keys.
- Work in progress: reduce token validation latency by caching JWKS for 5s instead of re-fetch per request in high-volume paths. Risk tradeoff discussed (staleness vs latency). Experiment to run starting 12/23.
- Action: add alert for JWKS fetch errors (owner: Sofia, due: 2026-12-24).

4) Quotas & throttling (Diego)
- Burst handling: spike on 12/19 overwhelmed soft quotas leading to a cascading backlog. Implemented quick fix: local short-term leaky-bucket smoothing in front of quota-adapter. Needs prod load testing.
- Proposal: introduce per-customer burst credits with decay to smooth scheduled jobs. Prototype design doc in PLT-4412. Feedback requested from product ops.
- Action: schedule load test (owner: Diego + SRE, due: 2026-12-27).

SRE / Oncall notes (Priya)
- Current oncall has quieter night profile but we saw flakiness during midday batch windows. Recommendation: run synthetic batch tests in off-peak to emulate customer job bursts.
- Playbook update: add step to check variant-cache TTL table during controlplane troubleshooting. Small doc patch in repo (LINK: https://github.com/redwood-inference/controlplane/pull/402).

Decisions made
- Defer aggressive prefetching of KV cache until we have more stable allocator behavior. Prefetching remains behind feature flag.
- Rollback of PR 389 stands until cache guard PR lands in staging and passes soak.
- Proceed with A/B routing canary but with stricter rollback condition: >1% increase in p95 or >0.3% user-visible error rate; immediate abort if detected.

Blockers / open questions
- Who will own the customer-notification for the quota-burst design? Product ops or Customer Success? (Action: Aisha to coordinate with CS, due: 2026-12-23)
- Need clarity on allowed TTL for JWKS caching given compliance constraints in EU customers. (Action: Sofia to confirm with security/compliance, due: 2026-12-24)
- Memory leaks on controlplane pods: we still see slow growth in heap over 48h in staging. Suspect recent metrics exporter change. (Owner: engineering-infra, follow up ticket: PLT-4499)

Action items (brief)
- Aisha: add variant-cache miss logs + instrument cache guard PR — due 2026-12-24.
- Liam: implement fallback-vs-primary routing metric and dashboard — due 2026-12-26.
- Sofia: add JWKS fetch-error alert and confirm EU TTL constraints with security — due 2026-12-24.
- Diego: run quota load test with SRE, capture tail latency and throttle events — due 2026-12-27.
- Priya: synthetic batch test plan and update playbook with cache-check step — due 2026-12-26.
- Aisha -> CS: coordinate customer communications around potential quota changes — due 2026-12-23.

Notes-to-self / informal fragments
- Short-term: be conservative with routing rebalances across zones during year-end traffic patterns.
- Keep an eye on the sidecar image pins; ephemeral CI candidate images slipped into staging last week. Nice to have: gating by digest.
- Question: would per-route sticky routing (sticky to variant for short TTL) help reduce variant churn? Quick experiment idea.

Follow-ups for next meeting (2026-12-29)
- Status check on PRs: cache guard, sidecar pin, JWKS alert, fallback metric.
- Results from Diego's load test + SRE observations.
- Canary A/B pre-rollout checklist final review (Liam).

Appendix: useful links and tickets
- PLT-4412 (burst credits design)
- PLT-4499 (heap growth investigation)
- ROUTE-1308 (sidecar image pin PR)
- PR 389 (rollback) & follow-up PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/controlplane/pull/389, https://github.com/redwood-inference/controlplane/pull/402

End of notes.

-- Aisha
